title: Tabernacle Construction
overview: Exodus 36 details the skilled craftsmanship and generous contributions of the Israelites in constructing the Tabernacle, the sacred dwelling place of God among His people. Under the leadership of Bezaleel and Aholiab, artisans empowered by divine wisdom meticulously create the curtains, coverings, boards, and other components as commanded by the Lord. The chapter highlights the abundance of offerings brought by the people, their obedience to Moses' instructions to cease contributions once sufficient materials were gathered, and the precise assembly of the Tabernacle’s structural elements. This chapter emphasizes the importance of divine guidance, communal participation, and faithful stewardship in worship, underscoring the holiness and glory of God’s presence in the midst of Israel.
structure:
**Verses 1-7: Divine Wisdom and Generous Offerings.** The chapter opens with the skilled work of Bezaleel, Aholiab, and other wise-hearted men empowered by God’s wisdom. The people bring abundant offerings for the sanctuary, prompting Moses to command a halt to further contributions as the materials are more than sufficient.

**Verses 8-19: The Curtains and Coverings.** Detailed descriptions are given of the making and coupling of the ten fine linen curtains with cherubim designs, the eleven goat hair curtains forming the tent, and the protective coverings of rams’ skins dyed red and badgers’ skins.

**Verses 20-30: The Boards and Silver Sockets.** The construction of the wooden boards of shittim wood for the Tabernacle’s sides is described, including their size, tenons, and the silver sockets that support them.

**Verses 31-38: Bars, Gold Overlay, and Hangings.** The chapter concludes with the making of the bars to hold the boards together, their gold overlay, the veil with cherubim, the pillars with gold hooks and silver sockets, and the embroidered hanging for the Tabernacle door.

keyVerses.text: Then wrought Bezaleel and Aholiab, and every wise hearted man, in whom the LORD put wisdom and understanding to know how to work all manner of work for the service of the sanctuary, according to all that the LORD had commanded.
keyVerses.significance: This verse establishes that the craftsmanship for the Tabernacle was divinely inspired, highlighting God’s direct involvement in equipping His people for worship. It underscores the theme of God-given wisdom enabling obedience to His commands.

keyVerses.text: And they spake unto Moses, saying, The people bring much more than enough for the service of the work, which the LORD commanded to make.
keyVerses.significance: This verse reveals the generosity and zeal of the Israelites in contributing to God’s work, demonstrating their wholehearted commitment to the sanctuary’s construction and their recognition of God’s provision.

keyVerses.text: And Moses gave commandment, and they caused it to be proclaimed throughout the camp, saying, Let neither man nor woman make any more work for the offering of the sanctuary. So the people were restrained from bringing.
keyVerses.significance: Moses’ command to stop contributions shows wise stewardship and obedience to God’s instructions, preventing waste and ensuring the work proceeds according to divine timing and sufficiency.

keyVerses.text: And he made fifty taches of gold, and coupled the curtains one unto another with the taches: so it became one tabernacle.
keyVerses.significance: This verse illustrates the unity and careful craftsmanship in assembling the Tabernacle, symbolizing the unified community of God’s people and the preciousness of the sanctuary.

keyVerses.text: And he overlaid the boards with gold, and made their rings of gold to be places for the bars, and overlaid the bars with gold.
keyVerses.significance: The gold overlay signifies the holiness and glory of the Tabernacle, reflecting God’s majestic presence and the sacredness of the dwelling place He commanded.

characters.name: Bezaleel
characters.description: A chief craftsman endowed by God with wisdom and skill to lead the artistic work on the Tabernacle. He plays a central role in executing the detailed instructions for the sanctuary’s construction.

characters.name: Aholiab
characters.description: An assistant artisan working alongside Bezaleel, also gifted with divine wisdom to contribute to the intricate work required for the Tabernacle’s furnishings and hangings.

characters.name: Moses
characters.description: The leader who oversees the project, receives the offerings from the people, and issues commands to regulate the contributions, ensuring the work aligns with God’s instructions.

characters.name: The Children of Israel
characters.description: The community who generously bring offerings and materials for the sanctuary, demonstrating their devotion and obedience in supporting the construction of God’s dwelling place.

themes.description: The chapter emphasizes that the artisans’ abilities are gifts from God, highlighting that true craftsmanship in worship is empowered by divine wisdom, reflecting God’s sovereignty over His sanctuary.
The abundant offerings from the people and the subsequent command to cease contributions illustrate the balance between generous giving and wise stewardship in fulfilling God’s purposes.
The detailed construction and use of precious materials like gold and fine linen signify the holiness of the Tabernacle, setting it apart as God’s dwelling among His people.
The chapter shows the collective involvement of the Israelites in building the sanctuary, underscoring the communal nature of worship and service to God.

historicalContext: Exodus 36 is set during the wilderness period following the Israelites’ deliverance from Egypt, traditionally dated to the 15th or 13th century BC depending on scholarly views. The Tabernacle construction occurs at Mount Sinai, a central geographical and spiritual location where God establishes His covenant with Israel. The artisans use materials and techniques common in the ancient Near East, such as shittim wood, fine linen, and metalwork, reflecting Israel’s cultural context. Politically, Israel is a nomadic community transitioning from slavery to nationhood under God’s direct guidance, with the Tabernacle serving as a tangible sign of God’s presence and leadership.

theologicalInterpretations.description: Reformed theology sees the Tabernacle as a typology of Christ and the church, with the skilled craftsmanship symbolizing the Spirit’s work in equipping believers for service. The chapter underscores God’s sovereignty in salvation and sanctification.

Dispensationalists emphasize the literal fulfillment of God’s instructions in the Tabernacle’s construction as foundational for understanding Israel’s unique covenant relationship, viewing the detailed work as a foreshadowing of future temple worship.

Early Church Fathers often interpreted the Tabernacle’s elements allegorically, seeing the curtains and coverings as symbols of Christ’s protection and the veil as the separation removed by His sacrifice, highlighting the sanctity of God’s dwelling.

The author describes the Tabernacle’s structure and furnishings, reflecting on their significance and fulfillment in Christ’s ministry.

application: Seek God’s wisdom and guidance in all tasks, recognizing that true skill and understanding come from Him.
Give generously and cheerfully to God’s work, but also practice wise stewardship and discernment.
Value and participate in the communal aspects of worship and service within the church body.
Recognize the holiness of God’s presence and approach worship with reverence and dedication.
Use your God-given gifts to serve the church and glorify God in practical ways.
Obey God’s instructions carefully, trusting His provision and timing in all endeavors.
conclusion: Exodus 36 stands as a powerful testament to God’s provision, wisdom, and the faithful response of His people in constructing a sacred space for His presence. Through divinely inspired craftsmanship and generous offerings, the Israelites demonstrate obedience and reverence, setting a pattern for worship that honors God’s holiness. This chapter encourages believers today to seek God’s guidance, contribute generously, and serve faithfully, recognizing that all gifts and talents are ultimately from the Lord and meant to glorify Him in community.
timeline: c. 1446 BC - Wilderness period following the Exodus from Egypt
